intuition.title: Study context: Atmosphere precedes sealed heating
intuition.text: Open-atmosphere mixing gives mixed cube-like populations and carbonate impurity; anaerobic glovebox mixing gives regular cubes. Both source treatments use 135 °C for18 h; the glovebox gas and hot pressure are unknown.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 2, Chemicals and synthesis of cube-like BaTiO3 nanoparticles; Main PDF p. 1–2, atmosphere-dependent morphology

intuition.title: Study context: Shape and phase are separate
intuition.text: Regular-cube shape does not uniquely establish a cubic polymorph. XRD uses a pseudocubic assumption while Raman indicates local tetragonal distortions; no measured atomic coordinates are supplied.

intuition.title: Study context: Size populations and aliquots
intuition.text: 20 nm is the air-route regular-cube subset;22 nm is the inert-route average edge;21.3 nm is Scherrer size. The separate21.5 nm FTIR caption and4.09 Å HRTEM spacing retain their own sample qualifications.

general_background.title: Carboxylic-acid and carboxylate ligands
general_background.summary: Carboxylic acids and carboxylates can associate with metal-containing surfaces and solution species through their oxygen groups. The hydrocarbon part of a long-chain ligand can favour dispersion in a compatible solvent, while acid-base equilibria influence how its head group associates.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Prospects of Colloidal Nanocrystals for Electronic and Optoelectronic Applications

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
